title: Arrogance
intro: Arrogance (kibr) – one of the worst qualities, and one that must never be found in a believer.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Allah (SWT) says that a person truly becomes arrogant as soon as they feel they need no one. <small>(Qur’an, Al-‘Alaq 96:6–7)</small>
One of the worst human qualities, which must never be found in a Muslim man or woman, is arrogance (kibr) – thinking you are better than others.

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) said: “No one who has even an atom’s weight of arrogance in his heart will enter Jannah.” A man said: “But a person likes his clothes and shoes to be nice.” The Prophet (SAW) said: “Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.” (Muslim)
So wanting to look neat is not arrogance. A person becomes arrogant the moment they leave the truth that comes from Allah (SWT) and His Prophet Muhammad (SAW), and when they look down on others.
The first one to become arrogant was Iblis, who said: “I am better than him – You created me from fire and created him from clay.” (Qur’an, Al-A‘raf 7:12)
A person also becomes arrogant when they feel they do not need others – or even Allah (SWT).

A believer knows that the wealth of this world does not last, that family background will mean nothing on the Day of Judgement, that knowledge is worth nothing if it is not for the sake of Allah, that beauty fades, and that our children will one day leave us too.

The Qur’an gives many examples of arrogant people: Fir‘awn (Pharaoh), Haman and Qarun from the time of Musa (AS), and Namrud from the time of Ibrahim (AS). Their arrogance was very dangerous. It was the reason Iblis was driven out of Jannah; Qarun and his huge wealth were swallowed by the earth; Fir‘awn and Haman drowned in the Red Sea – and all the arrogant will be humbled and led into Jahannam on the Day of Judgement.
A believer must guard against arrogance, because it brings no good in this world or the next. All of Allah’s servants are special and deserve attention and respect!

learn.text: Hadith: the three who were tested

learn.html: The Prophet (SAW) told that Allah wanted to test three men from the Children of Israel: one had a skin disease, one was bald and one was blind. Allah sent them an angel.

items: The angel asked the man with the skin disease what he wanted most. “Nice skin, so people don’t turn away from me.” The angel passed his hand over him and he was healed. He asked for camels, and was given a pregnant she-camel with the dua: “May Allah bless it for you.”
The bald man wished for nice hair. He was healed, asked for cows, and was given a pregnant cow with the same dua.
The blind man asked Allah to give him back his sight, so he could see people. He was healed, asked for sheep, and was given a sheep with the same dua.

learn.html: Their animals multiplied until each had a whole valley full: one of camels, one of cows and one of sheep.

Then the angel came back to each of them in the shape and look the man used to have, as a poor traveller who had lost everything on his journey, and asked for one animal for the sake of the One who had given them health and wealth.

items: The first man said: “I have too many costs.” The angel said: “Don’t I know you? Weren’t you the one people turned away from, and poor, and Allah gave to you?” He said: “No – I inherited this from my forefathers.” The angel said: “If you are lying, may Allah return you to how you were.”
The bald man answered in the same way, and got the same reply.

The man who had been blind said: “I was blind and Allah gave me back my sight. Take whatever you want and leave whatever you want. By Allah, I will not stop you from anything you take for the sake of Allah.”

learn.title: Hadith
learn.html: The angel said: “Keep your wealth! You were only being tested. Allah is pleased with you and displeased with your two companions.” (Bukhari)

practice.title: Arrogant people in the Qur’an
pairs: swallowed by the earth with his wealth

practice.title: The three who were tested
practice.prompt: Put the story in the right order.
items: Allah sends an angel to three men: one with a skin disease, one bald and one blind
Each is healed and given an animal with the dua for blessing
Their animals multiply until each has a whole valley
The angel returns as a poor traveller and asks for help
Only the man who had been blind is grateful and shares

practice.title: What is arrogance?
practice.prompt: Tap every example of arrogance, then tap Check.

options.text: 🙄 Refusing the truth because someone younger said it
😏 Thinking you are better because your family is richer
🗯️ Making fun of a classmate who reads slowly
🙅 “I don’t need anyone – not even Allah”
👕 Wearing clean, nice clothes to the masjid
options.why: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty – arrogance is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.

options.text: 🎓 Using your knowledge to help others
options.why: Knowledge used for the sake of Allah is good, not arrogance.

questions.q: What is arrogance, as the Prophet (SAW) explained?
options: Rejecting the truth and looking down on people

questions.q: Who was the first to become arrogant?

options: “I am better than him – You made me from fire”

questions.q: Why was the man who had been blind rewarded?
options: He was grateful and shared for the sake of Allah

questions.q: When does a person become arrogant, according to Surah Al-‘Alaq?
options: When they feel they need no one

practice.title: Questions and tasks
prompts: 🚪 How does a person fall into arrogance?
🔍 What do people become arrogant because of?
📖 Which examples of arrogance does the Qur’an give?
🐑 Task: read and talk about the hadith “The three who were tested”. Which man would you like to be like, and why?
